newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip ahead of jobs data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip ahead of jobs data.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities continued to lose ground on Thursday amid employment report jitters, mortgage-backed analysts said.
"We've seen a lot of selling (of pass-throughs) pretty much across the board on payrolls fears," one trader said.
Most trades were of small bundles of securities, she said.
Pass-throughs fell 1/32 to 8/32 by late afternoon, with yield spreads over Treasuries unchanged to somewhat tighter. Premium coupons fared best, slipping 1/32 to 3/32.
Despite the prevailing negative sentiment, some investors maintained a bullish outlook, one mortgage analyst said.
"People were taking all kinds of positions ahead of payrolls," he said.

The employment report scheduled for tomorrow morning at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT should show 244,000 new jobs were created in August as the unemployment rate slipped to 5.3 percent from 5.4 percent in July, said economists surveyed last Friday.
Such a report could push the Federal Reserve toward restraint but would not be enough to cause a credit tightening at the Fed's September 24 policy meeting, the economists said.
Late on Thursday, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons were off 5/32 at 99-25/32, yielding 114 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.
Comparable FNMAs were off 5/32 at 99-27/32, and FHLMCs were off 5/32 at 99-29/32.
The ten-year Treasury note was off 12/32 to yield 6.98 percent late in the day.
